# Water reference phase state

`eos.water_phase`

## Source

**Wagner, W.; Kretzschmar, H.-J. (2008); IAPWS (2007)**

The IAPWS-IF97 Gibbs formulation: Regions 1 and 2 as dimensionless functions of `pi = p/p*` and `tau = T*/T`, selected by the Region 4 saturation curve, differentiated for the full property set and converted mass-to-molar.


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `T` | K | absolute temperature |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `z_factor` | dimensionless | the compressibility factor `Z = P v/(R T)` |
| `u` | J/mol | the internal energy |
| `h` | J/mol | the enthalpy |
| `s` | J/(mol*K) | the entropy |
| `cv` | J/(mol*K) | the isochoric heat capacity |
| `cp` | J/(mol*K) | the isobaric heat capacity |
| `g` | J/mol | the Gibbs energy, `h - T s` |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure; zero and below are not states |

## Assumptions

- the fluid is pure water; the equation of state is the IAPWS-IF97 industrial formulation of NeqSim's `thermo.util.steam.Iapws_if97`, a Gibbs-energy form rather than the single Helmholtz form of the other reference equations.
- the region is selected by the Region 4 saturation curve: subcooled liquid (Region 1) at or below `Tsat(p)` and superheated vapour (Region 2) above it; Regions 3 (near-critical) and 5 (high-temperature) are not implemented in NeqSim and are not here.
- IF97 is mass-based: `R = 0.461526` kJ/(kg.K), pressure in MPa, and the properties specific; the model converts to the molar SI convention with the molar mass `M = 0.01801528` kg/mol.
- the isochoric heat capacity follows the exact identity `cv = cp + R (g_pi - tau g_pitau)^2 / g_pipi` in the reduced Gibbs variables, since NeqSim's class does not expose it.
